title: River flood gauge history for Montana locations: feasibility, terms and join rule
question: Can gauge flood history (NWS flood categories, observed history, USGS daily and instantaneous values, IEM flood warnings) support a per-location river flood record for Montana in the first version, and on what join rule and legal basis?
bottom_line: Feasible as a narrow first-version layer, not as a daily flood-day history. NWPS lists 277 Montana gauges; 102 define an NWS flood stage and 57 define all four categories. Billings (BILM8, USGS 06214500) has flood stage 13.5 ft and sits 2.0 miles from the town centre. The USGS annual peak stage record there runs 1963 to 2024; water year 2022 is the only year in 2021 to 2025 at or above flood stage (peak 16.37 ft on 2022-06-15 09:30 MDT). Neither USGS service carries a daily gage height series for this gauge, so 'days above flood stage per water year' has to come from 15-minute values. The requested USGS endpoint (waterservices.usgs.gov) is being shut down on 2027-02-22 and degraded from 2026-11-16; api.waterdata.usgs.gov answered every anonymous request tested. Only 17.3 percent of Montana land lies within 10 miles of a flood-stage gauge; 12 of the 14 towns in the repository's towns.json do.
recommendation: IN for the first version, narrowed: a 'river flood record at the gauge' line built only from (1) NWS flood categories and (2) USGS annual peak stage per water year, for the nearest flood-stage gauge within 10 miles, from api.waterdata.usgs.gov and NWPS (US federal works, public domain). OUT for v1: daily flood-day counts and 15-minute stage histories (no daily stage series; 2.75 MB raw JSON per gauge per water year). Per-address lines wait behind the same counsel gate as the other per-address layers (research README section 8.3, OW-H7); a per-town gauge table could ship first. Official flood warnings (IEM FL.W) are a separate lane: the June 2022 record is usable (14 products; every NEW product carries UGC codes and a LAT...LON polygon), but the IEM terms conflict, so take the NWS text or resolve IEM's terms first.

join_rule.pool: NWPS gauges (api.water.noaa.gov/nwps/v1/gauges) that define an NWS flood stage (minor category), any state, after the elevation-scale exclusion below; 271 gauges in the Montana wider box, 102 of them in Montana.
exclude: gauges with no flood stage defined (not_defined or -9999); this drops reservoir gauges that define only an action level

gauges whose NWS categories are elevations: any category of 1,000 ft or more (32 gauges in the wider box; 13 of them define a minor stage, all in Idaho, South Dakota or Wyoming, for example Lake Pend Oreille at Hope at 2,063.5 ft). These 13 are removed; the nearest of them to a Montana grid point is 13.7 miles (Lake Pend Oreille at Hope, HOPI1; grid 0.05 degree), the next 25.0 miles; no Montana gauge has this problem
gauges with no USGS number stay in the pool for the NWS stage but have no annual peak series (3 Montana gauges: ULLM8, KELM8, COTM8)
join_rule.distance: great-circle distance from the address point to the gauge point (NWPS latitude and longitude), nearest wins, cut-off 10 miles (16.1 km); beyond 10 miles no gauge line is shown
join_rule.display: gauge name, LID, USGS number, miles to one decimal, flood stage in ft, water-year peaks at or above flood stage
join_rule.words: River flood record at the {name} gauge, {miles} miles away; it does not say water reached this address.
join_rule.no_gauge_words: No gauge with an NWS flood stage is within 10 miles of this address. That is not a statement that the river did not flood here.
join_rule.kind_label: River gauge (a new kind word; separate from Official alert, Forecast and Report)
join_rule.time: store UTC; show water years (October 1 to September 30); show the gauge's local zone (MST7MDT) where a time of day is shown
join_rule.not_said: no damage, no roof, no insurance, no 'water reached'

june_2022_flood_days.mismatch_risk: In WY2021 to WY2025 the daily-mean and daily-peak rules flag the same days (0 peak-only days). On 2022-06-14 the peak was 1.29 ft above the daily mean and on 2022-06-15 0.95 ft; discharge daily mean was about 11 percent below the instantaneous peak. A daily-mean rule would understate a short crest; a daily-peak rule would overstate a few-minute spike. Use the annual peak for the record and state the peak's time.

open_questions: Owner: confirm the 10-mile cut-off (17.3 percent of Montana land; 12 of 14 repo towns) or choose 25 miles (69.6 percent) or 5 miles (4.8 percent).
Counsel (OW-H7): per-address river gauge lines are per-address output; confirm they wait behind the same gate as the hail and address layers.
IEM terms conflict (public domain disclaimer vs All rights reserved footer): pick the NWS text source for official flood warnings or get counsel's reading before any IEM-derived warning data ships.
USGS API keys and production rate limits: the docs say keys raise the limits; the limits were not read; 109 anonymous requests returned 200.
NWPS 'preliminary' codes (R, O) are not defined in the spec; crest dates are date-only at 00:00Z.
The NWPS observed window is about 30 days and date parameters are ignored; history must come from USGS.

The Benchland centre (47.075 N, 110.015 W) is from the B2 brief and is not confirmed (no Benchland row in the Census 2024 place file); the 10-mile result holds for any centre within a few miles because the nearest flood-stage gauge is 44 miles away.
Whether NWPS flood stages and USGS gage height share the same gauge datum was not reconciled (NWPS datum block not compared with USGS site datum).
Provisional data: WY2025 15-minute values at Billings are 20,205 of 35,039 provisional (P); recent years will change.
Missing data: 2022-07-14 and 2023-08-02 have no Billings stage values; 253 (WY2022) and 666 (WY2023) 15-minute intervals are missing.
IEM CGI: the phenomena filter was not applied with limitps=0; the alert archive counts for other years were not pulled (only June 2022).
NOAA-level terms pages returned 403; the NOAA-level public-domain statement is unverified.
The 14 Montana gauges on the Canadian border and the out-of-state gauges in the wider box were all fetched; the 271-gauge pool is the wider-box pool after the elevation-scale exclusion.
data_quality: NWPS detail for BILM8 lists usgsId 06214500 (not 06295000, which is Yellowstone River at Forsyth).
Billings flood stage 13.5 ft is confirmed by three sources: NWPS categories, the NWS text product (Flood stage is 13.5 feet) and the USGS-linked annual peak list.
The IEM FL.W rows match the text products on event numbers and NWSLI codes (checked for the 14 products).
NWPS 'historic' list and USGS annual peaks agree to 0.01 ft on the top eight crests.
